
### TCP segment format 

::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="TCP segment contents, showing (in order): (lower level header), source port (16 bits), destination port (16 bits), sequence number (32 bits), acknowledgment number (32 bits), data offset (4 bits), 4 unused bits, flag bits (CWR, ECE, URG< ACK, PSH, RST, SYN, FIN), window size (16 bits), checksum (16 bits), urgent pointer (16 bits), options (variable), data"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="source port, destination port (both 16 bits) highlighted"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="seuqence number (32 bits) highlighted"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="acknowledgment number (32 bits) highlighted along with ACK flag bit"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="window size (16 bits) highlighted"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-6.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6 fig-alt="urgent pointer (16 bits) and URG flag bit highlighted"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-7.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=7}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-8.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=8}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-9.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=9}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-tcp-segment-format.figure-10.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=10 fig-alt="data offset (4 bits) and options highlighted"}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2}

ports identify program/socket on machines<br/>
(we'll talk more when we cover sockets)

machines identified in lower-layer headers

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3}

byte number for first byte of data in this packet

:::

::: {.myoverbox .vlow .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4}

ack number = 1 + byte number of largest byte acknowledged <br/>
only meaningful if ACK 'flag' is 1

:::

::: {.myoverbox .high .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5}

* window size is receive window size <br/> tells sender how much receiver will accept

* sender window could/often will be different (not directly visible in packets)

:::

::: {.myoverbox .high .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6}

*  some fields releated to 'urgent data' mechanism 

*  almost never used today

:::

::: {.myoverbox .high .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=7}

PSH (push) 'flag' is hint that sender does not have more data to send right away

:::

::: {.myoverbox .high .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=8}

RST (reset), SYN (synchronize), FIN flags <br/>
used for connnection managemnet <br/>
(we'll talk more when we cover sockets

:::


::: {.myoverbox .high .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=9}

CWD (congestion window received) and <br/>
ECE (explicit congestion notification echo) flags<br/>
someties used as part of setting window sizes<br/>
to match network conditions (later topic for us)

:::

::: {.myoverbox .high .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=10}

* header can have variable number of "options"<br/>
  technically optional, but almost always used today

* size of header indicated by _data offset_<br/>
  (data offset is in  units of 32-bit words, not bytes)

:::


### exercise: maximum throughput  {.smaller}



* let's say we have a receiver window size of 65535 bytes
  * receiver window size is 16 bit field
* and a round-trip time of 100 ms 
<hr class="vspace" />
* if we want to avoid sending data the receiver may reject as outside its window, maximum throughput?
 <table>
<tr><td>A. around 32kbyte/sec</td><td>B. around 64kbyte/sec</td></tr>
<tr><td>C. around 128kbyte/sec</td><td>D. around 320kbyte/sec</td></tr>
<tr><td>E. around 640kbyte/sec</td><td>F. around 1280kbyte/sec</td></tr>
<tr><td>G. something else</td></tr>
</table>


### selected TCP options  {.smaller}


* window size scale factor 

   * allow receiver window sizes greater than 64k
   * needed to get reasonable bandwidth on modern networks

* timestamps 

   * allow figuring out round trip time to estimate timeout
   * extend 32-bit sequence number, which is too small for multi-gigabit networks

* selective acknowledgements 

   * allow providing information about ‘holes’ in received data
   * example: I got bytes 1--5000, 6000--7000, 8000--9000
   * without it would only say 5000

::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-selected-tcp-option-formats.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="TCP option format: 8-byte kind field; 8-byte length field; followed by option data. Two example options: window scale option: kind=3, length=3, 8-byte shift count field; timestamps option: kind=8, length=10, sender timestamp, echoed timestamp"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-selected-tcp-option-formats.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="highlighting the length field"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-selected-tcp-option-formats.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="highlighting the kind field"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-selected-tcp-option-formats.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="highlighting the window scale option, which contains a shift count field"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-selected-tcp-option-formats.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="highlighting the timestamp option, which contains a sender timestamp and echoed timestamp"}

![](/reliable-tcp/texfig/tcp-segment-basic-selected-tcp-option-formats.figure-6.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6 fig-alt="highlighting the echoed timestamp field"}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .vlow .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2}

length field permits skipping unrecognized options

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .vlow .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3}

unique kind codes for each option<br/>
from list maintained by IANA</br>
(Internet Assigned Numbers Authority)

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .low .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4}

*  sent only in connection setup 
*  only takes effect if both sides send it
*  set amount to left-shift all window size fields by

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .high .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=6}

*  echoed timestamp: only valid in ACK messages
*  copy of timestamp sent in message being ACK'd
*  allows computing round-trip-time

:::


### TCP connection setup preview 


* client$\rightarrow$server: SYN flag + seq=randomA [no data]
* server$\rightarrow$client: SYN+ACK flags  + seq=randomB ack=randomA+1 [no data]
* client$\rightarrow$server: ACK flags  + seq=randomA+1 ack=randomB+1 [no data]
